title: Doct. IV. In this practice we must be sincere and constant, I will keep it.

segments.text: 1. Having such an help as this continual Direction.

2. Such an engagement as this condescension to direct and warn a poor creature. And to the end, that is to the end of my life; there is no other period to our obedience but death. The Greek have it, 〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉, continually. The Word doth properly signifie the heel or soal of the foot; by traduction thence, the end of a thing, and sometimes a reward and recompence.
1. It is not enough to begin a good course, but we must go on in it if we mean to reach the Goal, else all our labour is lost; the end crowneth the work.

2. God that made us begin doth also make us to continue to the end. Is the beginning from God, the end and perfection from us? this is to ascribe that which is less perfect to God, and that which is more perfect to us.
